Requirement: Every product must pass 5 tests: (1) own identity, (2) own lifecycle, (3) 5+ unique business attributes, (4) natural domain owner, (5) semantic uniqueness.
Example: A real standalone table must have its own identity, lifecycle, several unique attributes, a natural home, and be distinct. A bare 'status_code' table of just id, name and code fails and should become an attribute on its parent.

Name: SSOT Violation Detection
Requirement: Same-name products across domains AND industry synonyms (e.g., customer/client, invoice/bill) are SSOT violations.
Example: The same concept under different names in different areas is a duplication problem. A `customer.profile` and a `client.profile` describe the same party, so pick one authoritative home.

Name: Overlap Threshold for Merge
Requirement: Products with 60%+ attribute/purpose overlap across domains trigger MERGE_TO_SHARED with discriminator column.
Example: Two tables that mostly overlap across areas should be merged with a marker column. A customer interaction and a support interaction at 70% overlap merge into one shared interaction with a source-type marker.

Name: Overlap Threshold for Remove
Requirement: Intra-domain duplicates or products with 90%+ overlap where one is clearly redundant -> REMOVE.
Example: Within one area, near-identical duplicate tables should have the weaker one removed. Two `account` tables in the same area at 95% overlap mean removing the less complete one.

Name: Different Entity Types Protected
Requirement: Master data vs transactional data = NEVER duplicates. Different lifecycle stages = NOT duplicates. Parent vs child = NOT duplicates.
Example: Tables of genuinely different kinds are never duplicates. A master `customer` and a transactional `order`, or different lifecycle stages, are kept separate even if names look similar.

Name: Generic vs Specific Scope Guard
Requirement: If one product is GENERIC (shared.party) and another is DOMAIN-SPECIFIC (customer.profile), they are NOT duplicates.
Example: A generic shared table and a specific one are not duplicates. A cross-area `shared.party` and an area-specific `customer.profile` serve different purposes and both stay.

Name: Domain Merge Threshold
Requirement: If 5+ products have same/similar names across two domains -> flag as IDENTICAL_DOMAIN_PAIR for potential domain merge.
Example: When two areas share many similarly named tables, consider merging the areas. If 'customer' and 'client' both have account, profile, contact, address and preference, they are likely the same area.

Name: Merge Over Delete
Requirement: For cross-domain overlaps >=60% prefer MERGE_TO_SHARED with discriminator column rather than REMOVE.
Example: For overlaps across areas, prefer merging into a shared table over deleting. Across areas, combine into one shared table with a marker; within one area, deleting a true duplicate is fine.

Name: Mutual Exclusivity
Requirement: A product cannot be both 'product_to_keep' in one pair AND 'product_to_remove' in another pair.
Example: A table cannot be marked to keep in one comparison and to delete in another. If `account` is kept against `client_account`, it cannot then be removed against `billing_account`.

Name: FK Orphaning Check
Requirement: Before removing product P, check if other products have FK references to P. Removing P would orphan those FKs.
Example: Before removing a table, check whether others link to it. Removing `address` while ten tables link to it would break all those links, so it stays.

Name: Removal Confidence
Requirement: Product removals require >90% confidence that the item truly does not belong.
Example: Only remove a table when you are very confident it does not belong. When in doubt, keep it; removal needs strong justification.

Name: Discriminator Pattern
Requirement: When merging products from different domains, add a discriminator attribute (e.g., party_type, interaction_source_type).
Example: When merging tables from different areas, add a marker column to tell them apart. Merging a customer contact and a partner contact adds a 'contact_type' marker with values 'customer' and 'partner'.

Name: Unique Table Names per Domain
Requirement: No two tables within the same domain may have the same name.
Example: Two tables in the same area cannot share a name. The 'customer' area cannot have two tables both called `profile`.

Name: Consolidate Cross-Domain Tables
Requirement: When tables with the same name exist in different domains, consolidate if attribute overlap >=70%. If <70%, keep both but rename secondary with domain prefix.
Example: Same-named tables in different areas merge if they overlap a lot, otherwise both stay with one renamed. A sales order and a procurement order at 75% overlap merge; a customer device and an IoT device at 30% stay separate.

Name: No Bare/Prefixed Duplicate Product Pair in a Domain
Requirement: Within one domain, a bare product X and a concept-prefixed variant of the same entity (X and procurement_X) must not coexist; they are the same entity and must be merged to a single owner.
Example: Within one area, a plain table and a prefixed version of the same entity should not coexist. Holding both `goods_receipt` and `procurement_goods_receipt` is a duplicate; keep one.

Name: Method vs Channel
Requirement: payment_method (instrument: card, cash, check) vs payment_channel (interface: online, in-store, phone) - NOT duplicates.
Example: How someone pays and where they pay are different things. A payment method (card, cash, check) and a payment channel (online, in-store, phone) answer different questions and are both kept.

Name: ID vs Name
Requirement: customer_id (system identifier) vs customer_name (display label) - NOT duplicates.
Example: An identifier and a display name are different. `customer_id` is for matching records while `customer_name` is for showing to people, so both are kept.

Name: Target vs Actual
Requirement: sla_target_time vs sla_actual_time - NOT duplicates. Different measurement semantics.
Example: A target and the actual result are different. A service-level target time and the actual measured time are both needed to judge whether the target was met.

Name: Lifecycle Timestamps
Requirement: created_at, modified_at, approved_at, completed_at - NOT duplicates. Each is a distinct lifecycle event.
Example: Different lifecycle timestamps are not duplicates. `created_at`, `approved_at` and `completed_at` each mark a distinct moment in a record's life.

Name: Different Granularity
Requirement: scheduled_date (DATE) vs scheduled_start_time (TIMESTAMP) - NOT duplicates if different precision needed.
Example: A date and a precise time can both be needed. A scheduled date for calendar planning and a scheduled start time for precise timing are different and both kept.

Name: Model Breadth Scales With Industry Complexity
Requirement: The number of domains, products, and attributes must scale with the industry complexity (regulatory bodies, operational systems, distribution channels, product-hierarchy depth). A complex, regulated, multi-channel industry yields a broad model; when complexity is ambiguous, size UP toward the richer band, never down.
Example: A more complex, heavily regulated industry deserves a bigger model. When in doubt about complexity, lean toward the larger size rather than the smaller one.

Name: Sizing Validation Math (base × uplift ≥ tier total)
Requirement: Chosen domain×product params control BASE tables only; associations are added later. Params MUST satisfy `base_tables × association_table_uplift ≥ tier_minimum_total` (base_tables ≈ avg_domains × avg_products_per_domain; total_attributes ≈ total_tables × avg_attributes_per_product). Both ECM and MVM midpoints must be validated against tier total targets before finalizing.
Example: Make sure the chosen sizes actually add up to the target totals. The base tables times their expected growth should meet or exceed the overall target before finalizing.

Name: MVM Lightness From Fewer Tables, Not Thinner Attributes
Requirement: An MVM MUST NOT thin out attributes. Every MVM table carries the SAME attribute depth as the equivalent ECM table; MVM lightness comes ONLY from covering fewer domains and fewer tables per domain. An MVM must be a production-ready foundation. (Resolves the contradiction in the candidate set — the authoritative legacy statement is SAME depth.)
Example: A lightweight model has fewer tables, not shallower ones. Each table in a small model carries the same depth of detail as in a full model; it just covers fewer areas and tables.

Name: Resize Hits Absolute Volumetric Targets, Not Source Ratios
Requirement: Shrink (ECM→MVM) and enlarge (MVM→ECM) MUST land within ABSOLUTE target ranges (target domains, products/domain, ~target_total_tables ±tolerance%) regardless of source size, explicitly NOT ratios/multiples of the source. Shrink follows the mandatory elimination order: back-office domains → association tables → non-core tables → consolidate small domains → verify+add-back. Survivors stay non-siloed.
Example: Resizing aims at fixed target sizes, not multiples of the original. Shrinking or growing a model lands within absolute target ranges regardless of how big the source was.

Name: Resize Immutability Guarantees
Requirement: Shrink may ONLY keep or remove existing domains/products (never invent new ones; relocated products move only to surviving domains). Enlarge MUST retain ALL existing domains and products verbatim (no remove/rename/relocate) and only ADD new ones.
Example: Shrinking can only keep or drop existing tables, never invent new ones, while growing keeps everything and only adds. A shrink relocates surviving tables only into surviving areas.

Name: MVM Back-Office Domain Exclusion
Requirement: In an MVM (shrink), full back-office domains (from `back_office_domain_candidates`) are OUT OF SCOPE unless the user explicitly requires them — prefer zero tables from those domains. Operational references to people may remain only as a minimal actor/identity slice under `person_landing_domain`. Back-office is cut FIRST, before operations is trimmed.
Example: When shrinking, drop back-office areas first unless the user needs them. A minimal slice of people data may remain, but full HR or finance areas are cut before operations is trimmed.

Name: Thin-Domain Detection via Median
Requirement: Compute the median product count across all domains; any domain below 75% of the median is THIN and MUST be flagged to enrich or merge. This is a relative (median-based) test, distinct from the absolute min-products band.
Example: Compare each area against the typical area size and flag the unusually thin ones. An area with far fewer tables than the median should be enriched or merged.

Name: Deterministic Small-Overage Product Trim (≤3 above max)
Requirement: When a domain generates at most 3 products above its sizing max, the excess MUST be trimmed DETERMINISTICALLY by dropping the LAST products (LLM emits most-essential first) WITHOUT a validation error or retry. Distinct from the >15% hard-ceiling trim — a small-overage (N+1..N+3) auto-fix to avoid soft-accept retry exhaustion. Overage >3 still hard-fails with a reduce instruction.
Example: If an area is just a few tables over its limit, quietly drop the last, least essential ones rather than failing. Going only one to three over triggers an automatic trim; going far over still fails and is redone.

Name: user_sizing_override Flag Emission Contract
Requirement: When user vibes explicitly request a model size / table count / domain count / scope restriction outside normal tier ranges, the sizing-parameter output MUST set `user_sizing_override=true` and params reflect the user's intent; the code then relaxes guardrail clamping. Default false keeps tier guardrails active. This is the explicit signal that lets downstream caps demote to advisory.
Example: When the user explicitly asks for a specific size outside the normal range, honour it and relax the usual limits. Otherwise the standard size guardrails stay in force.

Name: Subdomain Count Range
Requirement: Min and max subdomains per domain defined by complexity tier. Never exactly 1 subdomain per domain.
Example: Each area is split into a sensible number of sub-areas, never just one. A typical area might have three to six sub-areas depending on the model's complexity.

Name: Exactly Two Words
Requirement: Each subdomain name must be EXACTLY 2 words. 1 word = rejected. 3+ words = rejected.
Example: A sub-area name is exactly two words. 'customer identity' is valid, while a single word like 'identity' is rejected.

Name: Min Products Per Subdomain
Requirement: Every subdomain must contain at least the minimum products per subdomain defined by the tier.
Example: Each sub-area must hold at least the minimum number of tables for its tier. A sub-area with only one table should be merged into another.

Name: No Overlapping Words
Requirement: No two subdomains within the same domain may share any word in their names.
Example: Two sub-areas in the same area cannot share a word. 'customer identity' and 'customer engagement' clash; use 'personal identity' and 'active engagement' instead.

Name: Business-Focused Names
Requirement: Use business terminology, NOT technical terms for subdomain names.
Example: Sub-area names use business language, not technical labels. 'account management' is good; 'table_group_1' is not.

Name: Balanced Distribution
Requirement: Products should be distributed as evenly as possible across subdomains within a domain.
Example: Spread tables roughly evenly across an area's sub-areas. With three sub-areas and twelve tables, aim for about four each rather than ten in one.

Name: No Placeholder Names
Requirement: NEVER use: 'Sub Domain1', 'Category 1', 'Group A', 'N/A', 'Other', 'General', 'Miscellaneous'.
Example: Sub-areas need real names, never placeholders. 'Group A', 'Other', 'Miscellaneous' or 'N/A' are not acceptable.

Name: No Subdomain Drift
Requirement: Each subdomain belongs to exactly ONE parent domain. No cross-domain subdomains.
Example: Each sub-area belongs to exactly one area. 'customer identity' lives only in its parent area and cannot span several.

Name: Self-Ref FK Must Create New Column
Requirement: When creating or renaming a self-referencing FK, the agent MUST create a new column with a hierarchical prefix (parent_, manager_, reporting_, etc.). It MUST NOT rename or overwrite the existing PK column. If the FK column name equals the PK name, the FK is always invalid and must be rejected.
Example: To make a table point to itself, add a new column with a relationship name; never reuse the identifier. A `category` table gets a new `parent_category_id`; you must not rename `category_id` itself.

Name: User-Vibed Links Protected from Bidirectional Removal
Requirement: FK links that were explicitly requested by the user via vibe instructions are protected from the bidirectional FK removal pass. When the QA stage detects A->B and B->A FK pairs, it MUST skip removal of any link flagged as user-vibed. User intent takes priority over bidirectional FK prohibition.
Example: A link the user specifically asked for is protected from automatic cleanup. If the user said 'link order to warehouse', that link stays even when the cleanup pass removes the reverse link.

Name: Untouched Tables Use IF NOT EXISTS
Requirement: During surgical deploy, tables that were NOT modified by the current vibe session MUST be deployed with CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS. Only tables that were actually touched by the vibe get full CREATE TABLE or CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE. This ensures surgical deploy is idempotent and safe for existing data.
Example: When updating just part of a model, leave untouched tables exactly as they are. A change to `order` rebuilds `order`, while `customer` and `product` are left alone so their existing data is preserved.

Name: Self-Reference Allowed by Role-Label OR Type-Matched Prefix
Requirement: A self-ref FK in-domain is allowed not only for the recognized hierarchical prefix list but also when the column has a recognizable role prefix/suffix AND its integer type matches the PK type (`_is_role_labeled_self_ref(attr_type, pk_type)`); otherwise BLOCKED at creation with "FK name must differ from PK".
Example: A self-link is allowed when its column has a clear role name and matches the identifier's type; otherwise it is blocked. A properly named parent or manager column is fine, a plain reuse of the identifier is not.

Name: Classification in Tags Only
Requirement: Data classification levels go in TAGS only, NOT in attribute names or descriptions. Consequently, attribute names must NEVER include classification prefixes like 'restricted_', 'confidential_', etc.
Example: Sensitivity belongs in the tags, not in the column name. An email field is named `email_address` and tagged as restricted personal data, not renamed 'restricted_email'.

Name: PII Tag Requirements
Requirement: MUST include specific PII tags: pii_email, pii_phone, pii_identifier, pii_address, pii_financial, pii_health, pii_biometric, pii_name, pii_dob, pii_national_id, pii_passport, pii_ip, pii_device.
Example: Personal data fields get a specific privacy tag. An email gets a personal-email tag, a national ID gets a national-identifier tag, and so on.

Name: No Structural Tags
Requirement: DO NOT include primary_key or foreign_key tags - these are structural, not classification.
Example: Do not tag columns as primary key or foreign key; that is structural, not a sensitivity label. Whether a column is a link is tracked separately from its tags.

Name: Sensitive Data is RESTRICTED
Requirement: PII (Personally Identifiable Information), PHI (Protected Health Information), and PCI (Payment Card Industry data) MUST ALL be tagged as 'restricted' with a specific PII/sensitivity tag. This is non-negotiable for regulatory compliance (GDPR, HIPAA, PCI-DSS).
Example: Personal, health and payment data must always be marked restricted with a specific tag. A name, an email, a diagnosis and a credit card number each get the restricted label plus their specific sensitivity tag.

Name: CONFIDENTIAL for Non-PII
Requirement: Use 'confidential' only for sensitive business data that is NOT PII/PHI/PCI.
Example: Use 'confidential' for sensitive business data that is not personal. Salary bands, internal pricing or trade secrets are confidential, but personal data is restricted instead.

Name: Empty Tags for Regular Data
Requirement: For regular operational data (status fields, codes, non-sensitive identifiers), leave tags EMPTY.
Example: Ordinary operational fields need no sensitivity tag. An `order_status`, a product category code or a `warehouse_id` are left untagged.

Name: Custom User Tags
Requirement: If user vibes request custom tags (key=value), MUST add to EVERY applicable attribute. User tags always take priority.
Example: If the user asks for a custom tag, apply it to every field it applies to, and let it take priority. 'tag all customer columns with source=crm' means every customer field gets that tag.

Name: No Reserved Characters in Tags
Requirement: Individual tag values must not contain reserved characters. Use underscores instead.
Example: Tag values use only plain characters and underscores. 'pii_email' is valid; 'pii-email', 'pii.email' or 'data=sensitive' are not.

Name: Org Contact PII Tagging
Requirement: Organizational contact data (facility addresses, office phone numbers, branch locations) MUST be tagged as 'confidential' even when not personal PII. Business contact information represents sensitive operational data that requires access control.
Example: Business contact data like office addresses and phone numbers is marked confidential even though it is not personal. A facility address or office phone gets the confidential label, not the restricted one reserved for personal data.

Name: Custom Tag Physical Persistence
Requirement: Custom tags defined in user vibes MUST persist through the full pipeline to physical Unity Catalog tables via ALTER TABLE SET TAGS and ALTER TABLE ALTER COLUMN SET TAGS SQL statements. Tags must appear in both the logical model (model.json) and the physical deployment.
Example: Custom tags the user defines must follow through to the actual deployed tables, not just the design. A request to tag all patient tables with 'compliance=hipaa' must end up applied on the real tables.

Name: FK Attribute Carries a Business Glossary Term
Requirement: Every FK attribute must carry a business-glossary term derived from its column name and a description naming the target entity and the business reason for the link.
Example: Every linking column needs a friendly name and a description of what it connects and why. A `billing_address_id` reads as 'Billing Address (link)' and explains it points to the address used for billing.

Name: Vibe Deviation Justification
Requirement: User vibe instructions are the highest authority for model decisions. The agent MUST follow vibe instructions or explicitly justify any deviation in the model architect review. Silent non-compliance is forbidden. Justifications must reference a specific modelling rule that conflicts with the vibe.
Example: The user's instructions are the top authority, and any deviation must be explained, not silent. If the user asked for five areas but the model has four, the review must state which two were merged and why.

Name: Vibe-Version Write Barrier
Requirement: On any 'vibe modeling of version' operation, the agent MUST write to a NEW model version (v+1), NEVER overwrite the source version in place. _assert_vibe_version_advances() MUST guard every metamodel write callsite (model.json save, _metamodel.business UPSERT, domain/product/attribute writes, JobTags update). The barrier raises if it detects the destination version equals the source version. (v0.8.3 R1 / v0.8.4 4th callsite)
Example: Re-modelling an existing version writes a new version rather than overwriting the old one. Starting from version 1 produces version 2, and version 1 stays intact for comparison.

Name: Scoped Run Refused on a Stale Base
Requirement: A 'vibe modeling of version' run with vibe_scope Some Domains or Some Subdomains MUST NOT build on a base that is behind the head version, the latest completed version of the business and scope whose deploy_status is not dry_run. Such a run is refused before it changes anything, with an error that names the base and the head; the check runs again before model.json is written. A Dry Run version never counts as head, and a run with a blank model_version never picks a Dry Run version as its base. An All Domains run may still build on an older version; lineage.base_version records the base it branched from.
Example: If version 4 is the latest version, a run scoped to the billing domain must start from version 4. Started from version 3 it is refused, because everything outside billing would come from version 3 and silently lose what version 4 changed. A dry run saved as version 5 does not count as the latest version.

Name: Catalog Teardown Drops Only Owned Schemas
Requirement: At setup, a 'vibe modeling of version', 'shrink ecm' or 'enlarge mvm' run MAY clear old schemas from the target catalog, but only schemas this business owns, meaning schemas that a version of this business whose deploy_status is not dry_run registered in _metamodel.domain. The teardown MUST NOT run on a Dry Run (run_type Dry Run), in a scoped run (vibe_scope Some Domains or Some Subdomains), or in a 'vibe modeling of version' whose base is the latest installed version of the catalog; that run keeps the owned schemas and its deploy plan replaces only the tables it changes. When the new model needs a schema name that already exists in the catalog and is not owned by this business, a Full Run MUST be refused before anything is dropped; a Dry Run only warns because it deploys nothing.
Example: A vibe run for the airlines business clears only the airlines schemas from its catalog. If another team's 'finance' schema sits in the same catalog and the new model also needs a 'finance' schema, the run stops with an error rather than dropping the other team's tables.

Name: Metric View Has Measures and Dimensions
Requirement: A metric view must define at least one measure (an aggregation such as a sum, count, or average) and at least one dimension (a grouping such as region, month, or category). A metric view left with no measure, or no dimension, is invalid and must not be kept.
Example: A "Sales by Region" metric view needs at least one number to measure (total sales) and at least one way to group it (region). An empty view with only a name, nothing to add up, or no grouping is not a real metric view and should be dropped.

Name: Metric View Built on a Single Declared Source
Requirement: A metric view is defined over one declared source product, and every measure and dimension it uses must be a column that physically exists on that source product. It must not silently pull columns from unrelated tables.
Example: A "Monthly Revenue" view built on the invoice table can only add up and group by columns that exist on invoice, like amount and invoice_date. It cannot use a region column that lives on the customer table unless that relationship is properly modeled.

Name: Named KPIs Are Built As Specified
Requirement: When the business names a specific KPI or metric view together with its intended measure and grouping, the model must include a metric view with that exact name, that measure, and those dimensions, not a renamed or empty stand-in.
Example: If the business asks for a "Vacancy Rate by Division" KPI, the model must contain a view named "Vacancy Rate" that computes the vacancy rate grouped by division, not an auto-named view like headcount_by_org that measures something else.

Name: Respect the Requested Metric-View Count
Requirement: When the business says how many metric views it wants (for example, "exactly three"), the model contains that many, limited to the requested set. Extra auto-generated metric views beyond what was asked for are not added.
Example: If the request is for exactly three dashboards, the model should have those three and no more. It should not silently add eighteen auto-generated per-table metric views nobody asked for.

Name: Business-Meaningful Metric View Names
Requirement: A metric view name clearly describes what it measures in business terms. Generic, technical, or auto-generated stub names are not acceptable.
Example: Name a view "Monthly Revenue by Region" so anyone immediately knows what it shows. Avoid vague names like mv1, metric_view_a, or a raw copy of a table name that says nothing about what is being measured.

Name: Authoritative Deterministic Gates
Requirement: Structured quality is enforced by DETERMINISTIC static gates that read the real model dict (and, post-build, the physical catalog). For every VREQ class that maps to a gate (glossary/division/subdomain/PII/type/PK/FK/description), the deterministic gate verdict is AUTHORITATIVE and OVERRIDES the LLM verifier verdict. The scoreboard cannot false-negative (artifact present but scored missing) or false-positive (missing but scored present).
Example: gov_transport base-MVM had 3031 glossary tags + 7 subdomain tags physically present, yet the LLM verifier scored them FAILED off a lossy snapshot. The deterministic gate reads the dict, sees 100% coverage, and reports fulfilled - overriding the lie.

Name: Every Table Has a Primary Key
Requirement: Every table (data product) MUST declare at least one primary-key attribute. A table with no PK is a hard gate failure routed to the agentic repair loop.
Example: Table 'customer.account' with no is_primary_key attribute -> missing_pk finding -> SelfFixer adds the PK.

Name: Every FK Targets a Valid PK
Requirement: Every foreign_key_to reference MUST resolve to an existing target product whose referenced column is that product's primary key. Dangling FKs, FKs to non-PK columns, and FKs to missing products are gate failures.
Example: FK 'order.customer_id -> customer.account.id' is valid only if customer.account.id is a PK. If it points to a non-PK or missing target it is flagged broken_fk/pk_mismatch.

Name: FK and Target PK Same Type
Requirement: A foreign-key column MUST have the same base data type as the primary-key column it references. Type mismatches (e.g. STRING FK to BIGINT PK) are gate failures.
Example: order.customer_id BIGINT -> customer.account.id BIGINT is valid. order.customer_id STRING -> customer.account.id BIGINT is fk_pk_type_mismatch.

Name: Glossary Term Tag Coverage
Requirement: When a business glossary is in use (any attribute carries a glossary tag, or the vibe requests one), EVERY business attribute (excluding PK and FK columns) MUST carry a glossary-term tag. Coverage below 90% is a gate failure routed to repair.
Example: If glossary tagging is active, attribute 'patient.encounter.diagnosis_code' must have a *_business_glossary_term tag. Untagged business columns -> missing_glossary_tag.

Name: PII Sensitivity Tag Coverage
Requirement: Every attribute whose name matches a person-data pattern (name/email/phone/ssn/dob/address/national_id/...) MUST carry a PII/sensitivity/classification tag. Person-pattern columns without a sensitivity tag are gate failures.
Example: 'customer.contact.email' must carry a pii/sensitivity tag. An untagged 'ssn' column -> pii_tagging_missing.

Name: Every Domain Has a Division Tag
Requirement: Every domain MUST carry a non-empty division tag. A domain with no division is a gate failure.
Example: Domain 'maintenance' with division='' -> missing_division_tag -> SelfFixer assigns operations/business/corporate.

Name: Division Within Canonical Set + Balance
Requirement: Every division value MUST be within {operations, business, corporate} (QGATE invalid_division otherwise). Corporate must stay <=20% of all domains (division_imbalance otherwise), per DOM-RUL-001.
Example: 6/10 domains tagged corporate -> division_imbalance. division='ops_support' -> invalid_division.

Name: Every Table Has a Subdomain Tag
Requirement: Every table MUST carry a non-empty subdomain grouping tag. Tables without a subdomain are gate failures.
Example: Table 'finance.invoice' with subdomain='' -> missing_subdomain_tag.

Name: Descriptions Present and Non-Placeholder
Requirement: Every domain, table, and attribute MUST have a description. Descriptions that are missing, placeholders (tbd/n/a/todo/none/-), echoes of the name, or shorter than 10 chars are gate failures (missing_*_description / low_quality_description).
Example: attribute 'order.line.qty' with description='qty' (echo) or 'tbd' -> low_quality_description -> repair loop rewrites it.

Name: Descriptions Within Width
Requirement: Every domain, table, and attribute description MUST be <= 256 characters and end on a complete word (never truncated mid-word). The pre-static-analysis autofix trims over-width descriptions on a word boundary; the deterministic gate reports any residual (description_over_width) to the repair loop. UC column-comment hard limit is 65535 chars; 256 keeps descriptions concise and readable.
Example: An FK justification cut with reasoning[:200] ended mid-word ('... rate case prudency d'); the width autofix re-trims it to <=256 on the last full word.

Name: Gates Wired Into Agentic Repair Loop
Requirement: Every structured gate category MUST be in the SelfFixer fixable whitelist so a discovered failure is automatically requeued and repaired within the agentic loop (not merely reported). Curated completeness categories (descriptions, tags, types) are queued even at info severity.
Example: missing_glossary_tag/missing_division_tag/missing_subdomain_tag/fk_pk_type_mismatch/low_quality_description all appear in _v366_sa_findings_requeue _fixable and reach SelfFixer.

Name: Physical-Parity Gate
Requirement: After the physical build, a parity gate MUST compare the live catalog (information_schema column_tags/columns/tables and the _metrics schema) against model.json. Any artifact declared in model.json but missing physically (dropped tags, dropped columns, dropped metric views) is a gate failure - this is the ground-truth anti-lying check.
Example: model.json declares 15 metric views; SHOW TABLES IN cat._metrics returns 13 -> physical-parity failure (2 metric views dropped at install).

Name: Scoped Run Changes Nothing Out of Scope
Requirement: When vibe_scope is Some Domains or Some Subdomains, every out-of-scope domain record, product, attribute and metric view, and the model-level metadata, MUST stay identical to the base model. The only exceptions are the permitted boundary deltas P1-P5: FK re-link, FK unlink, link to a product created in scope, authorized new FK column, and substitution of renamed in-scope table and column names in a metric view. Any other out-of-scope addition, removal or change is a vibe_scope_out_of_scope_change finding. Only fields that model.json stores count; working fields such as is_primary_key, nullable and classification are not changes. The deterministic fence repairs it: checkpoints restore the base record, and the serialize gate splices the out-of-scope sections from the base model.json and fails closed (model.json is not written) if a change remains. The category is deliberately excluded from the SelfFixer _fixable list in _v366_sa_findings_requeue. This is a documented exception to QGATE-RUL-011 (Gates Wired Into Agentic Repair Loop): an LLM repair could edit frozen tables. All Domains runs never raise it. Inside the scope a VOV changes only the products and whole domains its requirements name; every other in-scope base product is frozen like an out-of-scope one (P1 re-links allowed), unless a requirement names a set, the whole model or no target. The serialize gate copies those products from the base, their metric views and the schema tags of a frozen domain record are kept at deploy, and the _vibe_scope block records the named products so an install applies the same rule.
Example: vibe_scope='Some Domains', business_domains='billing'. A naming pass renames out-of-scope column 'customer.account.acct_status' -> vibe_scope_out_of_scope_change -> the fence restores the base column; SelfFixer never sees it.

Name: Scoped Run Blocks Changes That Break Out-of-Scope Artifacts
Requirement: When vibe_scope is Some Domains or Some Subdomains, an in-scope change MUST be blocked, with outcome scope_dependency_conflict, when it would break an out-of-scope artifact in a way P1-P5 cannot repair. The blocked cases: dropping an in-scope table or column that an out-of-scope metric view reads; renaming an in-scope column that such a view reads when the new name cannot be substituted in the view SQL (P5 re-points a rename it can substitute); changing the type of an in-scope primary key that out-of-scope FKs reference; moving a product across the scope boundary in either direction. An in-scope table that out-of-scope FKs reference and that disappears or moves without a ledger drop or rename is an unrequested_drop_of_referenced conflict. A residual is a vibe_scope_dependency_conflict finding. The deterministic fence repairs it: the mutation gate rejects the change, the architect review drops any proposal that would remove, rename, merge, split or move a referenced in-scope product without a ledger drop, checkpoints roll back a cross-boundary move, an unrequested drop is restored from the base model (or moved back) with a WARN and recorded in the run outcomes, and the serialize gate fails closed if a conflict remains. The category is deliberately excluded from the SelfFixer _fixable list in _v366_sa_findings_requeue. This is a documented exception to QGATE-RUL-011 (Gates Wired Into Agentic Repair Loop): an LLM repair could edit frozen tables.
Example: Out-of-scope metric view 'sales_revenue_mv' reads in-scope table 'billing.invoice'. A vibe asks to drop billing.invoice -> scope_dependency_conflict -> the table stays and the requirement is reported as blocked.

Name: Scoped Run Leaves No Dangling Boundary FK
Requirement: When vibe_scope is Some Domains or Some Subdomains, an out-of-scope FK column whose in-scope target was renamed, moved or dropped MUST NOT keep the stale foreign_key_to. A stale reference is a vibe_scope_dangling_boundary_fk finding. The deterministic boundary reconciler repairs it from the run's fence ledger, and only as a consequence of an explicit in-scope change recorded there with its cause (requirement id or deterministic operation): P1 re-points the FK to the target renamed or moved by a ledger rename and keeps the column name and type; P2 clears foreign_key_to when the target table was dropped by a ledger drop and keeps the column. P3 links an unlinked column only to a product created by a ledger create. The category is deliberately excluded from the SelfFixer _fixable list in _v366_sa_findings_requeue. This is a documented exception to QGATE-RUL-011 (Gates Wired Into Agentic Repair Loop): an LLM repair could edit frozen tables.
Example: Out-of-scope 'order.sales_order.invoice_id -> billing.invoice.invoice_id' after in-scope billing.invoice is renamed to billing.customer_invoice -> vibe_scope_dangling_boundary_fk -> the reconciler re-points it (P1). Had the table been dropped, it clears foreign_key_to and keeps the column (P2).

Name: Scoped Run Keeps New Products in Listed Subdomains
Requirement: When vibe_scope is Some Subdomains, every new product in a listed domain MUST use one of the subdomains listed for that domain (the 'domain.subdomain' entries in business_domains). A new product in an unlisted subdomain is a vibe_scope_subdomain_violation finding. The deterministic fence repairs it by removing the product with remove_product_and_references. A new in-scope product with no subdomain is never removed: in a VOV it gets the only subdomain listed for its domain, otherwise the constrained subdomain allocation assigns one, otherwise the run fails with a clear message; a failed allocation halts the run before model.json is written. In a new base model, the products of unlisted subdomains are pruned the same way right after subdomain allocation. The category is deliberately excluded from the SelfFixer _fixable list in _v366_sa_findings_requeue. This is a documented exception to QGATE-RUL-011 (Gates Wired Into Agentic Repair Loop): an LLM repair could edit frozen tables.
Example: vibe_scope='Some Subdomains', business_domains='billing.invoicing'. A new product 'billing.collection_case' lands in subdomain 'collections' -> vibe_scope_subdomain_violation -> the fence removes it and its references.

Name: Scoped Run Adds No Unlisted Domain
Requirement: When vibe_scope is Some Domains or Some Subdomains, the model MUST NOT gain a domain that is neither in the base model nor in the business_domains scope list. A new base model has an empty base, so every domain outside the listed roster counts. Such a domain is a vibe_scope_extra_domain finding. The deterministic fence repairs it by dropping the domain and its products. The category is deliberately excluded from the SelfFixer _fixable list in _v366_sa_findings_requeue. This is a documented exception to QGATE-RUL-011 (Gates Wired Into Agentic Repair Loop): an LLM repair could edit frozen tables.
Example: vibe_scope='Some Domains', business_domains='billing, payment'. Missing-parent creation adds a new domain 'reference' -> vibe_scope_extra_domain -> the fence drops it and its products.

Name: Rename Leaves No Original Behind
Requirement: A rename MUST replace the product, not duplicate it. After a rename the old name is gone, the new name exists, the primary key follows the new name, and every foreign_key_to that pointed at the old product points at the new one. A post-condition checks this wherever a change is accepted (LLM sandbox, deterministic path, parallel merge, SelfFixer) and rejects a change that leaves the old product behind. A residual pair is a rename_leftover_original finding: two products in the same domain where the rename ledger records one renamed to the other (followed through later domain renames), or one name extends the other at a word boundary. Overlap is the Jaccard index of business columns, so the primary key, history and housekeeping columns do not count. A name-extension pair is an error at 70% overlap or more; a ledger pair is always reported, as an error at 70% or more and as a warning below. A rule-based autofix merges only error-level pairs: it keeps the new name, moves the leftover's extra columns and FKs onto it, drops the leftover and records the merge in the change and rename ledgers. In a scoped run it merges only pairs whose both sides are in scope and reports the others without changing them. The category is in the SelfFixer _fixable list and _ACTIONABLE_CATEGORIES in _v366_sa_findings_requeue, per QGATE-RUL-011 (Gates Wired Into Agentic Repair Loop).
Example: A vibe asks to rename procurement.livestock_procurement to livestock_procurement_allocation. The run adds procurement.livestock_procurement_allocation but keeps procurement.livestock_procurement with almost the same columns, and operations.feedlot_intake.livestock_procurement_id still points at the old product -> rename_leftover_original -> the autofix drops the leftover and re-points the FK. purchase_order next to purchase_order_line (column overlap 0.2) is not flagged.

Name: model.json Matches the Canonical Model
Requirement: Immediately before model.json is written, a deterministic parity gate MUST verify, for every product outside the vibe_scope fence, that the product has an attribute named after its primary key, that every foreign_key_to resolves to an existing product and column, and that the model.json attributes (keys and count) and FK edges equal the canonical in-memory model that the DDL and the _metamodel tables are built from. It repairs once: a missing primary key is restored from memory (or created with the configured PK suffix), an FK whose column is gone is re-pointed to the target's primary key or cleared, and model.json-only changes are written back to memory so the physical schema follows. A violation that survives the repair fails closed: model.json is not written and the run halts before carry-over or deploy. Out-of-scope products are left to the vibe_scope fence (QGATE-RUL-013/015), so pre-existing dangling FKs in a frozen base stay as they are. No pass may delete a primary-key attribute because of an FK, normalization or dedupe decision; it may only clear foreign_key_to. The static-analysis broken_fk check also flags an FK whose target table exists but lacks the referenced column; broken_fk and pk_attribute_missing are in the SelfFixer _fixable list per QGATE-RUL-011.
Example: An FK semantic gate drops customer.campaign.campaign_id (the table's primary key) because it judged the column's FK to product.campaign invalid, leaving 11 FKs to customer.campaign.campaign_id dangling. The PK guard clears only the FK; if any pass still loses the column, the parity gate restores it from memory before the write, so model.json, the DDL and the _metamodel tables all keep 3180 attributes.

Name: VOV Changes Only What the Vibe Names
Requirement: In a vibe modeling of version with vibe_scope All Domains, the run MUST change only the entities its vibe names, plus the FK dependencies P1 to P5. Right after extraction the requirement targets become a 'requested' fence: a named product (d.p or d.p.column), a domain named on its own, every product carrying a bare name, and the new names a named rename, move or split creates. Every other base product is frozen with all its columns, autofix and finalize passes cannot change any base product, and static-analysis findings on base entities go to next_vibes instead of the repair loop. A set, model-wide or empty target turns the fence off for the run with a WARN (vov-strict-requested-off). A Full Run on the installed head keeps the data of every table it does not change: the deploy plan replaces changed tables only, from the fence facts or, with the fence off, from a diff against the base model.json.
Example: A vibe adds customer.gift_card and a column to order.sales_order. The cross-domain collision autofix may not rename product.campaign to product_campaign, the p016/p73i passes may not rename columns of untouched products, and the naming pass may not rename the user's new column sku.season_code to sku_season_code; each such change is restored before model.json is written.

Name: Domain Schema Carries Its Own Name
Requirement: A domain's database_name MUST carry the domain's own name under the model naming convention (an optional schema prefix or suffix is allowed). A database_name that names another domain is a domain_database_name_mismatch finding: the domain's tables would deploy into that other schema. The finding is routed to the SelfFixer, and a deterministic domain rename rewrites database_name by replacing the old name inside it, so a prefix or suffix survives.
Example: Domain 'client' with database_name 'project' (left by a merge of project into client) is flagged; 'dbx_client' passes; after renaming vendor to partner, 'dbx_vendor' becomes 'dbx_partner'.

Name: Table Name Is a SQL Identifier
Requirement: Every product's table_name MUST be a plain SQL identifier (letters, digits and underscores, not starting with a digit). A table_name with a dot, a space or another character is an invalid_table_name error: its DDL cannot create the table, so the product silently disappears from Unity Catalog. The finding is routed to the SelfFixer, and no LLM fallback mutation may write such a value into table_name or primary_key.
Example: table_name 'product.carrier' (written by a corrective that copied a qualified reference) is an error; 'carrier' passes.
